questions.question: The term 'Tripitakas' in Buddhism mean three:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Baskets__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tripiṭaka **is a Sanskrit word meaning **Three Baskets**.
 
• It is the traditional term used by **Buddhist traditions** to describe their **various canons of scriptures**.
 
• The expression **Three Baskets** originally referred to three receptacles containing the scrolls on which the **Buddhist scriptures **were originally preserved. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__**Some important terms used in Buddhism are:**__

 
• **Buddha**. - `Buddha` means `an enlightened person.
 
• **Dhamma**. - The truth about what life is really life.
 
• **Sangha**. - The community of Buddhists.

questions.question: The earliest Buddhist texts were written in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pali.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• The earliest Buddhist texts were written in **Pali.**
 
• The Early Buddhist texts were divided into two categories- Pali and Anupali texts.
 
• Pali texts :
 
 
• Tripitaka, Deep Vansha, Maha Vansha, and Milind Pannaho are important texts.
 
• Tripitaka is the earliest and most important text in pali.
 
 
 
• Anupali texts (Sanskrit and other texts) :
 
 
• Divyavadan, Aryamanjushrimulkalpa, and Lalit Vistar are the important texts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Tripitaka **(Pali Canon), Mahayana Sutras and the Tibetan Book of the Dead are three significant no canonical Buddhist writings.
 
• The Pali Canon, which signifies “the expression of Buddha,” incorporates a portion of the Buddha’s talk, however, it additionally consolidates the lessons of his students.

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Vinaya Pitaka** is a book related to the rules of the Buddhist Sangha.
 
• The Vinaya was preserved by being memorized and chanted by generations of monks and nuns.
 
• The Vinaya-Pitaka, or "basket of discipline," is the first of three parts of the Tipitaka, a collection of the earliest Buddhist texts.
 
• The Vinaya records the Buddha's rules of discipline for monks and nuns. 
 
• It also contains stories about the first Buddhist monks and nuns and how they lived.
 
• The Vinaya was not written down during the Buddha's lifetime.

questions.question: Where did Buddha give the last sermon before his Mahanirvana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kushinagar**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lord Buddha gave his last sermon at the Kushinagar __district of Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Since then Kushinagar became the place of Buddhist pilgrimage.
 
• **Kushinagar **is also known as Kusinara, as it is home to many pilgrimages for Buddhism followers in India and worldwide.
 
• **Ramabhar Stupa in Kushinagar **was built with a portion of the Buddha's ashes on the place where his cremation took place.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Buddha was an ordinary person named Siddhartha Gautama, whose profound insights inspired the world.
 
• He was born into the royal family of the Sakya clan who ruled from Kapilvastu, in Lumbini which is situated near the Indo-Nepal Border.
 
• At the age of 29, Gautama left home and rejected his life of riches, and embraced a lifestyle of asceticism or extreme self-discipline.
 
• After six years of hardship, Gautama attained Bodhi (enlightenment) under a pipal tree at Bodhgaya a village in Bihar.
 
• Buddha gave his first sermon in the village of Sarnath, near the city of Benares in UP.
 
 
• This event is known as Dharma-Chakra-Pravartana (turning of the wheel of law).
 
 
 
• He died at the age of 80 in 483 BCE at a place called Kushinagara a town in UP.
 
 
• The event is known as Mahaparinibban.

questions.question: Which of the following was a compilation of the teachings of Buddha in around 5th to 4th century BCE?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tipitaka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Tipitaka is a collection of Buddhist teachings that are the foundation of the** Theravada Buddhist philosophy**.
 
• It's the earliest grouping of **Buddhist teachings.**
 
• The Tipitaka is also known as the **Tripitaka**, from the Pali words, ti, meaning "**three**," and Pitaka, meaning "**baskets**."
 
• Theravada Buddhism describes the Tripitaka as **Buddhavacana** or the word of the Buddha, as it contains the teachings of the Buddha and his disciples.
 
• The content was gathered and organized at the **First Buddhist Council**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• ​Gautam Buddha was the founder of Buddhism and is revered by Buddhists as a fully enlightened being who taught a path to Nirvana.
 
• Besides "Buddha" and the name Siddhārtha Gautama, he was also known by other names and titles, such as **Shakyamuni ("Sage of the Shakyas").**
 
• **Gautam Buddha:**
 
 
• Born: Lumbini Province, Nepal
 
• Died: Kushinagar
 
• Full name: Siddhartha Gautama
 
• Spouse: Yasodhara

questions.question: The 'Digha Nikaya' is a collection of ______ discourses.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Buddhist.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Digha Nikaya** is a **Buddhist scripture**, the first of the five-strong Nikayas, in the Sutta Pitaka, which is one of the three baskets that compose the Pali Tipitaka of Buddhism. 
 
• Digha Nikaya which means the long collection, a Sanskrit Dirghagama that contains 34 long suttas including doctrinal expositions, legends, and moral rules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Buddhism started in India over 2,600 years ago as a way of life that had the potential of transforming a person.
 
• It is one of the important religions of South and South-Eastern Asian countries.
 
• The religion is based upon the teachings, life experiences of its founder Siddhartha Gautam.
 
• Major Buddhist Texts -
 
 
• The Vinaya Pitaka consists of rules of conduct and discipline applicable to the monastic life of the monks and nuns.
 
• The Sutta Pitaka consists of the main teaching or Dhamma of Buddha. It is divided into five Nikaya or collections:
 
• Majjhima Nikaya
 
• Digha Nikaya
 
• Samyutta Nikaya
 
• Anguttara Nikaya
 
• Khuddaka Nikaya
 
• The Abhidhamma Pitaka is a philosophical analysis and systematization of the teaching and scholarly activity of the monks.
 
• Other important Buddhist texts include Divyavadana, Dipavamsa, Mahavamsa, Milind Panha, etc.
